shared.concept_anchor: Dual-designation areas — Tiger Reserve and Elephant Reserve overlap

en.display_text:
With reference to the governance relationship between Tiger Reserves and Elephant Reserves in India, consider the following statements:

1. Areas simultaneously designated as both Tiger Reserves and Elephant Reserves exist in India — such overlap is legally permissible.
2. In areas that are simultaneously Tiger Reserves and Elephant Reserves, the legal protections and enforcement mechanisms of the Tiger Reserve designation take precedence and govern land use within the overlapping area.
3. The Central Government provides equal budgetary allocations for tiger conservation and elephant conservation under their respective flagship schemes.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?

(a) 1 and 2 only
(b) 2 and 3 only
(c) 3 only
(d) 1, 2 and 3

statement_analysis.statement: Areas simultaneously designated as both Tiger Reserves and Elephant Reserves exist in India — such overlap is legally permissible.
statement_analysis.reason: Several areas like Corbett, Nagarhole, and Bandipur carry both Tiger Reserve and Elephant Reserve designations simultaneously; the two designations are not mutually exclusive.

statement_analysis.statement: In areas that are simultaneously Tiger Reserves and Elephant Reserves, the legal protections and enforcement mechanisms of the Tiger Reserve designation take precedence and govern land use within the overlapping area.
statement_analysis.reason: Since Tiger Reserve notifications under Section 38V of WPA carry statutory enforcement authority (through NTCA), while elephant reserve designations lack equivalent statutory backing, the stronger Tiger Reserve legal framework effectively governs such overlapping areas.

statement_analysis.statement: The Central Government provides equal budgetary allocations for tiger conservation and elephant conservation under their respective flagship schemes.
statement_analysis.reason: Tiger conservation under Project Tiger receives significantly higher budgetary allocation than elephant conservation under Project Elephant — the funding is demonstrably unequal despite both being CSSs.

en.strong_distractor: d — Option (d) 'All three correct' tempts students who accept the dual-designation and precedence claims as true and don't have specific knowledge of the budgetary disparity between the two projects.
elimination_logic: Verify Statement 1: Corbett, Nagarhole, Bandipur — all are dual-designated; legal overlap is permissible — Statement 1 is correct.
Verify Statement 2: Tiger Reserve's statutory framework (Section 38V/NTCA) governs overlapping areas because it has stronger legal teeth than elephant reserve guidelines — Statement 2 is correct.
Test Statement 3: 'Equal budgetary allocations' — tiger conservation consistently receives more funding than elephant conservation; this claim is false — Statement 3 is incorrect.
Statements 1 and 2 correct, Statement 3 incorrect — answer is (a).
en.upsc_trap_explanation: Statement 3 contains a partial-truth: both Project Tiger and Project Elephant are Centrally Sponsored Schemes (CSS) — this true fact is then extended with the false claim of 'equal allocation.' Students who know both are CSS schemes may accept the equal funding claim without having specific budget data. The disparity in funding is well-documented but requires more detailed study than the basic scheme classification.
en.final_explanation:
The governance overlap between Tiger Reserves and Elephant Reserves is an important and frequently examined distinction.

• Statement 1 — Correct: Dual designation is legally permissible and exists in practice. Corbett Tiger Reserve and Elephant Reserve, Nagarhole, and Bandipur are commonly cited examples where both designations apply to the same landscape.
• Statement 2 — Correct: In overlapping areas, the Tiger Reserve's statutory framework under WPA Section 38V (enforced through NTCA) takes effective precedence over elephant reserve guidelines because the former carries enforceable legal authority while the latter does not. This means the stronger legal protection governs.
• Statement 3 — Incorrect: Project Tiger consistently receives significantly higher central funding than Project Elephant. Both are CSS schemes, but tiger conservation enjoys a much larger budgetary allocation — a documented inequality in India's wildlife conservation spending.

Value Addition:
• The dual-designation reality means some of India's best-protected forests simultaneously serve as tiger and elephant habitats.
• India has 53 Tiger Reserves (as of recent counts) and approximately 33 Elephant Reserves — there is significant geographic overlap.
• Budgetary asymmetry is one reason conservationists have sought a statutory authority for elephant conservation equivalent to NTCA.

भारत में बाघ अभयारण्य और हाथी अभयारण्य के शासन संबंध के संदर्भ में, निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार करें:

en.display_text:
Under Project Elephant, India conducts systematic elephant population estimation exercises ________, with the most recent large-scale census having been completed in 2017, estimating approximately 27,312 wild elephants in the country.

(a) Annually
(b) Every 5 years
(c) Every 3 years
(d) Every 10 years
en.strong_distractor: c — Option (c) is deceptive because students may remember a census was conducted around 2012 or know India conducts different wildlife censuses at different intervals, and 3 years sounds plausible for a major species.
elimination_logic: The elephant census in India is conducted every 5 years — this is a documented institutional fact under Project Elephant.
Eliminate (a): Annual census would be logistically impractical for a species scattered across ~76,000 sq km — not the established interval.
Eliminate (c): A 3-year interval is plausible-sounding but incorrect — the established periodicity is 5 years.
Eliminate (d): A 10-year interval would align with national population census — but wildlife censuses operate on a shorter cycle of 5 years.
Confirm (b): Every 5 years is the correct elephant census interval under Project Elephant.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: The temporal-swap trap offers four plausible census intervals. Students who do not specifically know the 5-year periodicity may choose 3 years (too frequent but plausible) or 10 years (confusing it with the decadal population census). The trap is that multiple timeframes are plausible at first glance, and only specific knowledge of Project Elephant's census periodicity produces the correct answer.
en.final_explanation:
India conducts systematic elephant population estimation exercises under Project Elephant at a fixed periodic interval.

• Option (a): Annual — Incorrect. Annual censuses of elephants would be logistically and financially impractical across ~76,000 sq km of elephant reserves; this is not the established interval.
• Option (b): Every 5 years — Correct. India's elephant population census is conducted on a 5-year cycle under Project Elephant. The most recent large-scale census in 2017 estimated approximately 27,312 wild elephants.
• Option (c): Every 3 years — Incorrect. Three-year intervals are not the established periodicity for elephant population estimation under Project Elephant.
• Option (d): Every 10 years — Incorrect. A decadal cycle would create excessively large data gaps for conservation management; the established interval is 5 years, not 10.

Value Addition:
• The 2017 census used dung DNA analysis alongside traditional right-of-way counts — a methodological advancement.
• The last census before 2017 was conducted in 2012, giving the 5-year pattern: 2007 → 2012 → 2017.
• Population trends from successive censuses inform Project Elephant's reserve management decisions and funding allocations.

प्रोजेक्ट एलीफेंट के तहत, भारत व्यवस्थित रूप से हाथी जनसंख्या अनुमान अभ्यास ________ करता है, जिसमें सबसे हाल की बड़ी जनगणना 2017 में पूरी हुई, जिसमें देश में लगभग 27,312 जंगली हाथियों का अनुमान लगाया गया।

(a) वार्षिक
(b) हर 5 वर्ष
(c) हर 3 वर्ष
(d) हर 10 वर्ष
hi.strong_distractor: c — विकल्प (c) भ्रमित करने वाला है क्योंकि छात्र याद रख सकते हैं कि लगभग 2012 में जनगणना हुई थी या जानते हैं कि भारत विभिन्न वन्यजीव जनगणनाएँ अलग-अलग अंतराल पर करता है, और 3 वर्ष एक प्रमुख प्रजाति के लिए संभावित लगता है।
elimination_logic: भारत में हाथी की जनगणना हर 5 वर्षों में की जाती है — यह प्रोजेक्ट एलीफेंट के तहत एक प्रलेखित संस्थागत तथ्य है।
(a) को हटाएं: वार्षिक जनगणना लगभग 76,000 वर्ग किलोमीटर में फैली प्रजाति के लिए व्यावहारिक नहीं होगी — यह स्थापित अंतराल नहीं है।
(c) को हटाएं: 3-वर्षीय अंतराल संभावित लगता है लेकिन गलत है — स्थापित आवृत्ति 5 वर्ष है।
(d) को हटाएं: 10-वर्षीय अंतराल राष्ट्रीय जनसंख्या जनगणना के अनुरूप होगा — लेकिन वन्यजीव जनगणनाएँ 5 वर्ष के छोटे चक्र पर संचालित होती हैं।
(b) की पुष्टि करें: हर 5 वर्ष प्रोजेक्ट एलीफेंट के तहत सही हाथी जनगणना अंतराल है।

hi.final_explanation:
भारत प्रोजेक्ट एलीफेंट के तहत एक निश्चित आवृत्ति पर व्यवस्थित हाथी जनसंख्या अनुमान अभ्यास करता है।

• विकल्प (a): वार्षिक — गलत। लगभग 76,000 वर्ग किलोमीटर के हाथी अभयारण्यों में वार्षिक जनगणना व्यावहारिक और वित्तीय रूप से संभव नहीं है; यह स्थापित अंतराल नहीं है।
• विकल्प (b): हर 5 वर्ष — सही। भारत की हाथी जनसंख्या जनगणना प्रोजेक्ट एलीफेंट के तहत 5-वर्षीय चक्र पर होती है। 2017 में हुई हाल की बड़ी जनगणना में लगभग 27,312 जंगली हाथियों का अनुमान लगाया गया।
• विकल्प (c): हर 3 वर्ष — गलत। 3-वर्षीय अंतराल प्रोजेक्ट एलीफेंट के तहत स्थापित आवृत्ति नहीं है।
• विकल्प (d): हर 10 वर्ष — गलत। दशकीय चक्र संरक्षण प्रबंधन के लिए अत्यधिक बड़े डेटा अंतराल बनाएगा; स्थापित अंतराल 5 वर्ष है, 10 नहीं।

• 2017 की जनगणना में पारंपरिक राइट-ऑफ-वे गणनाओं के साथ मल डीएनए विश्लेषण का उपयोग किया गया — एक विधिगत उन्नति।
• 2017 से पहले अंतिम जनगणना 2012 में हुई थी, जिससे 5-वर्षीय पैटर्न बनता है: 2007 → 2012 → 2017।
• लगातार जनगणनाओं से प्राप्त जनसंख्या प्रवृत्तियाँ प्रोजेक्ट एलीफेंट के अभयारण्य प्रबंधन निर्णयों और वित्त पोषण आवंटन को सूचित करती हैं।
